notes: Corrected: both *side of the house* phrases write two *the*s against the two article morphemes standing in them, so each article takes the one before its own word — the article on הַיְמָנִית / הַשְּׂמָאלִית takes the *the* written before *right* / *left*, and the construct כֶּתֶף keeps only *side*. Rule 47's third sentence rules this expressly, a present article morpheme taking the written *the* before a supplied one does even where the head noun is a construct that could take none of its own; 2CH.23.20 applies the same rule to `שַׁעַר הָעֶלְיוֹן` → *the upper gate*. The accepted alignment had supplied a *the* on כֶּתֶף and left both agreement articles unrepresented.

*along by* is taken as one rendering of the first לְ, headed on *by*; the second לְ, for which the ASV writes nothing before *and the house*, is unrepresented under rule 40. The marginal literal glosses *shoulder* were read and set aside under rule 38.
